result.summary: Round 3 result: both assigned round-2 issues are corrected as scoped. 17-fix-review-privacy-cache:1 holds. The `java.net.URI` strictness is gone for the reported triggers: space, `{}`, `[]`, and a bare `%` in path or query. The quoting is validation-only, and the original endpoint is returned unchanged. 18-fix-review-expiry:1 holds under the selected reload-and-authoritative-inspection remedy. The expired post-send dead end is not silently unlocked or replayed. Both clients show a fixed message telling the user to reload and inspect a fresh registration snapshot. I found three remaining defects independently. (1) MED: the new Kotlin lexical authority check misses credential-bearing endpoints that WHATWG `new URL` rejects, because special-scheme URLs can omit or vary the `//`. This is a Kotlin/TS parity gap. (2) LOW: some endpoints that TS accepts still make `java.net.URI` throw in Kotlin. (3) LOW: the recovery guidance has no cross-client parity or text test, and the Kotlin text is a duplicated literal.

findings.trigger: A safe read, list row or public patch carries an `http`/`https` endpoint whose authority does not follow a literal `//` immediately after the scheme. Examples: `https:user:pw@host/`, `https:///user:pw@host`, `https:/\tab/user:pw@host`, `https:\\user:pw@host`.
findings.defect: The new check looks for `@` only when the text literally starts with `//` after the first `:`, and the authority ends at the first `/`, `?` or `#`. WHATWG `new URL` has different rules for special schemes. It tolerates missing or extra slashes, treats `\` as a slash, and strips TAB/LF/CR. It then parses `user:pw` as credentials, so TS refuses these endpoints. In Kotlin the authority is empty or the URI is opaque, so `'@' in authority` is false and `URI.rawUserInfo` is null. The endpoint is accepted with embedded credentials. This reopens the original credential-bypass class for special schemes and is a TS/Kotlin parity gap. The same rules also over-refuse in Kotlin: `https://host\@x/` has no credentials under WHATWG but is refused here (conservative direction).
findings.evidence: Lines 220-224 compute `authorityStart` only when `endpoint.startsWith("//", schemeEnd+1)`. Lines 228-229 quote the tail and then `URI(...)`, which yields an opaque or empty-authority URI with null `rawUserInfo`. The supplied negative cases are only `postgresql://secret:password@...`, `redis://:pw@my_host:6379` and `postgresql://u:p@a:1,b:2/db`. All have a literal `//`. No supplied test covers a missing, extra or backslash slash form. The WHATWG behaviour is my knowledge of the spec and of Node's `URL`, not supplied evidence.
findings.remedy: Mirror the WHATWG special-scheme rules lexically. Strip TAB/LF/CR first. For `http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss` and `ftp`, skip any run of `/` or `\` after `:` and end the authority at `/`, `\`, `?` or `#`. For other schemes, keep the `//` rule. Reject `@` in the resulting authority. Add Kotlin and TS parity fixtures for the forms above. Better still, put them in the shared wire corpus so both languages are driven by one list.

findings.trigger: A WHATWG-valid endpoint that still contains characters `java.net.URI` rejects after the current quoting. Examples: a second `#` in the fragment (`https://host/#a#b`), DEL or C1 controls, Unicode space separators such as U+00A0 or U+2028 in the path or query, or `{`, `}` or `"` in the host.
findings.defect: The quote set is `% U+0000-U+0020 < > " { } | \ ^ ` [ ]`. It omits `#` after the first `#`, U+007F-U+00A0 and the other Unicode space or control characters. The authority is passed to `URI` raw. WHATWG accepts or percent-encodes all of these. `URI` throws and `checked{}` converts that into `ConnectionReplyException`, so one row refuses the whole `list()` result and a patch is refused. This is the same failure shape as 17-fix-review-privacy-cache:1, on a narrower set of inputs.
findings.evidence: The quote regex on line 228. The added tests cover only space, `{value}`, `[value]` and a bare `%`. That `java.net.URI` rejects the remaining characters is my JDK knowledge, not supplied evidence.
findings.remedy: Do not depend on `java.net.URI` for acceptance. Check the scheme with `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:` and apply the lexical authority check. Or widen the validation-only quoting to every non-ASCII, control and non-first-`#` character. Add parity fixtures for each class.

findings.trigger: A future edit changes the `reconciliation-required` recovery wording in one client only.
findings.defect: The reload guidance is a duplicated string literal. VS Code has it in `messages.ts`; the Kotlin panel has an inline `when` literal. No supplied test asserts that the expired post-send path produces this errorCode and message in either client, or that the two texts match. The round-2 remedy asked for a parity test, and the Kotlin live UI is stated as deferred. Drift would silently remove the only exit instruction for a permanently blocked key. Two things are also not in the supplied evidence: the Kotlin controller path that sets `errorCode` (round-2 cited lines 261 and 279) and where the renderer's `problems` object comes from.
findings.evidence: messages.ts line 1 and ConnectionsManagerPanel.kt line 96 hold identical text by inspection only. The renderer uses `problems[r.errorCode]` at line 176 with no visible definition. The test list shows no assertion on the message. The existing test, per round 2, asserts only the busy and `reconciliation-required` states.
findings.remedy: Add a parity test that drives submit, not-seen and expiry, then Reconcile or Replay, in both clients. It should assert `errorCode==='reconciliation-required'`, that the rendered text equals the shared constant, and that `submit` still throws `busy`. Prefer one shared message source (the corpus) for both clients.

obligations.evidence: The Kotlin `URI` parse no longer sees raw space, `{}`, `[]` or a bare `%`: the tail is quoted at line 228 for validation only. Lines 228-229 build a local `uri`, and the original endpoint is returned untouched. Tests at ConnectionProtocolTest.kt lines 102-107 assert `https://host/?q=a b`, `?q={value}` and `/[value]?q=100%` are accepted by `safeConnection`, `list` and `publicPatch` with the value preserved. Line 108 keeps `https://bad host/` refused, matching TS. The TS test at lines 69-72 has the same fixtures. The reported run shows 6 Kotlin protocol tests passing. Residual strictness and the special-scheme credential gap are reported as separate findings.

The approved policy is explicit reload-and-authoritative-inspection guidance, with no new dismiss protocol. controller.ts line 166 maps not-seen plus expired to `reconciliation-required`. Line 168 sets `errorCode='reconciliation-required'`. Replay at line 180 does the same and sends nothing. `canReplay` and `canDismiss` stay false and the key stays blocked, so there is no silent unlock or replay. messages.ts and the Kotlin panel line 96 both show: 'Check the original operation. If it remains unresolved, reload the workbench or Project, then refresh and inspect the registration before any new explicit action. Its historical outcome is unknown; never repeat it automatically.' The LLD section 3.6 and the recovery narrative document the same reload exit and say a pre-send expired ticket remains dismissible. Check the renderer's `problems` binding and the Kotlin controller's `errorCode` assignment against the source; neither is in the supplied evidence (see the LOW finding and evidenceRequests).

limitations: No tools were run. Test passes come from the supplied narrative and TAP output. The TAP block with 1..6 tests is not attributable to a specific file, so I could not tie it to the TS wire test, which has 4 tests.
WHATWG URL and java.net.URI behaviours cited in the findings are my knowledge, not supplied evidence.
Kotlin ConnectionMutationController and the renderer's `problems` definition were not supplied.
Controller.ts lines 111-148 were not supplied, so other paths that set `reconciliation-required` were not examined.
Kotlin live UI is deferred by the supplied narrative.
evidenceRequests: Kotlin ConnectionMutationController (status and replay expiry handling, errorCode assignment)
vscode-plugin/src/connections/renderer.ts definition of `problems`, and the host-to-webview binding to CONNECTION_PROBLEMS
Shared-corpus or test output for the special-scheme credential forms (`https:user:pw@host/`, `https:///user:pw@host`, backslash and TAB variants) in both languages
